angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 605,259 km at 134.85 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.4159 +/- 0.0143 mas (same row, RUWE 0.95): 134.85 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.87 +/- 0.06 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HAT-P-3 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 605,259 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.06 +/- 0.28 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HAT-P-3 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5185 +/- 80 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-3 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-3 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hat-p-3.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.584, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-3 (pscomppars): spectral type K1, from Bourrier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A..63B/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HAT-P-3: main object type Em*, Emission-line Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-3 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.27 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-3 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.36, from Ment et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..213M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-3 (pscomppars): age 1.6 Gyr, from Ment et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..213M/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-3 (pscomppars): rotation period 19.9 d, from Bourrier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A..63B/abstract)

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/705/A142/tablea1 (Physical properties study of planet systems), column Prot: 19.6 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HAT-P-3 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 0.46 km/s, from Bourrier et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A..63B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.87 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.208. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
